answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds each identity to cryptographic stake burning via a quadratic burn function where verifying $k$ concurrent identities requires burning $O(k^2)$ tokens. Like an immovable basalt bedrock, this creates inescapable economic friction with superlinear attacker cost. An attacker cannot cheaply spawn nodes that wander across clusters; even a nimble sparrow node requires an exponential deposit hierarchy to participate.
